about.title: About Mobin Bartar
about.description: More than two decades of industrial print production for publishers, industry and institutions.

story.title: Our story
story.description: Mobin Bartar started in 2000 with a single two-colour offset press. Today, with eight active production lines and 140 staff, it is a well-established name in Iranian industrial printing. That growth came from steady investment in machinery and technical training — not from rapid, unplanned expansion.

precision.title: Precision
precision.description: Every job is produced against documented parameters so the next run matches the last one.

reliability.title: Reliability
reliability.description: The delivery date we state is the date we hold ourselves to.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.description: Specifications, stock and costs are agreed in writing before production starts.

investment.title: Technical investment
investment.description: Press renewal and operator training are a permanent part of our annual plan.

certifications.title: Standards & certifications
certifications.description: Our quality control follows recognised printing-industry standards.

facility.title: The facility
facility.description: Our 6,500 square-metre plant operates in Tehran's Print & Publishing Industrial Park.

about.intro: Mobin Bartar is an industrial printing company in Tehran, producing for publishers, industry and public organisations since 2000.

capabilities.title: Production capability
capabilities.description: Capacity determines which jobs can be accepted without subcontracting and without a drop in quality.

quality.title: Quality control
quality.description: Every job is produced against documented parameters. Colour profile, stock, press settings and spectrophotometer readings are archived, so a reprint matches the original.

equipmentSection.title: Machinery

founded.title: The beginning
founded.description: The company started with a single two-colour offset press and five staff in south Tehran.

expansion.description: Moving to the Print & Publishing Industrial Park tripled capacity and brought binding in-house.
